cultural.vision_reason: A pair of fringed silk lamba landy fotsy shawls with woven-in geometric and floral motifs, the classic white silk shawl type made and worn by Merina weavers of the Highlands; this is a well-documented Merina textile form.

physical.title: Pair of shawls (Lamba Landy Fotsy)
physical.summary: A lamba is an untailored textile worn by all ages, classes, and genders across much of Madagascar. This is an example of a woman’s garment made after Queen Ranavalona II made Christianity the state religion of the Merina Kingdom. Soon after, all-white lamba became popular for both Sunday church and daily wear. Fotsy is white in the Malagasy language. Indicating its owner’s worldliness, the white-on-white patterns alluded to fashionable imported textiles with damask patterns.

location.made_in_place: unknown weaver (French Madagascar or Malagasy Republic), Merina style
